purpose: opacity, lifecycle and leakage probes for M2-S1 blocker S1-B12 against the Core-side random mapping-ID reference prototype (threshold ruling T5.4)

scenarios.note: the Core-side table maps the ID back correctly for the trusted caller
IDs are unlinkable per path, constant-length, and contain no path fragment under any tried codec

scenarios.adversary_holds: all issued ID strings (and nothing else)
attempts: substring match of every path/resource fragment against every ID
base64url/base64/base32/hex/raw decodes of the random segment
md5/sha1/sha256/sha512 hex and b64 of rel, backslash rel, file name and rid
scenarios.note: inductive evidence: the exercised analysis space recovers nothing (see limitations)
every guess returns the same typed REF_UNKNOWN_ID; no oracle distinguishes near-misses
the caller-visible surfaces carry events and stable codes only -- no rel, no rid, no table rows
expired mappings stay typeable and unreachable (ruling T6 semantics)
revocation is immediate on next resolve (ruling T6); the opened-consumption carve-out is a runtime concern outside this prototype
touch() re-arms the TTL; idle references expire (ruling T6 sliding renewal)

boundary_summary.opacity: no path or resource id recoverable from ID strings across the exercised analysis space (M-02/M-03); guessing is uniform-typed (M-04)
boundary_summary.leakage: errors, logs and telemetry carry no mapping-table entries (M-05)
boundary_summary.lifecycle: expiry, revocation and sliding renewal are typed (M-06/M-07/M-08)

limitations: Opacity is inductive evidence: a bounded analysis space (substrings, common codecs, hash dictionaries, 5k+ guesses, neighbour mutations) recovers nothing from 192-bit random IDs. This is not a cryptographic proof and not a product guarantee.
The mapping table lives inside the Core process by construction; protecting Core memory, crash dumps or a compromised host is out of scope (ruling T5 makes the host a trusted layer).
No product IPC runtime, Tauri command or React consumer exists behind these surfaces; the log/telemetry streams here are prototype-level stand-ins for the caller-visible output.
Core restart / table persistence semantics (S1-B5) are not exercised.
